notes: Extra fields beyond SCHEMA.md: every level carries 'J' and every transition 'lower_J' / 'upper_J', because NIST gives identical energies for several fine-structure pairs (all nF doublets; Li nP for n >= 3; Na 7D, 8D ...) so that energy alone cannot identify the component. 'lifetime_alternatives' lists other sourced values; 'rme_J_ea0' is |<n l J||D||n' l' J'>| in e*a0 in the Safronova / ARC getReducedMatrixElementJ convention (symmetric in the two levels; A_ki = 2.02613e18 * rme^2 / (lambda_Angstrom^3 * (2J_k+1))). rme with method 'theory' are relativistic all-order values of the Safronova group from the UDel portal (the portal attaches no experimental reference to them); where the same transition is printed in the group's magic-wavelength paper, that printed value is given under rme_J_ea0.alternatives. 'branching' is the portal's theoretical branching fraction of that decay channel of the upper level. No A_s is given: NIST ASD already carries A_ki for these atoms. Theory lifetimes are purely radiative (0 K). frequency_THz refers to the isotope named in its 'isotope' field (hyperfine centre of gravity); frequencies of the other isotopes are under frequency_THz_<A>. Isotope shifts are nu(first) - nu(second). Hyperfine constants are the 'Recommended' / weighted-average rows of Allegrini et al. 2022 unless the source string says otherwise; entries flagged sign_unknown are absolute values. ionization_energy is an extra top-level block. Na: the D-line reduced matrix elements in Steck's sheet use the convention <J||er||J'> = rme/sqrt(2J+1) of the lower level, i.e. smaller by sqrt(2); they are listed under alternatives with that stated. The 4D lifetime of Kandela (50.7(5) ns) is 3 sigma below theory.
